source.text: Ἐὰν ταῖς γλώσσαις τῶν ἀνθρώπων λαλῶ καὶ τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, γέγονα χαλκὸς ἠχῶν ἢ κύμβαλον ἀλαλάζον.

records.literal_gloss: If in the tongues of the men I speak and of the angels, love but not I have, I have become bronze echoing or cymbal clanging.

en.L: If I speak in the tongues of {{gender:human beings|men}} and of angels, but do not have love, I have become echoing bronze or a clanging cymbal.
en.B: Suppose I speak in the tongues of {{gender:human beings|men}}, and of angels too. If I do not have love, I am no more than booming bronze or a clashing cymbal.
en.R: I might be able to speak in tongues, in the languages of people and even of angels. But if I do not have love, I am only empty noise, like banging metal or a crashing cymbal.

fr.L: Si je parle les langues des {{gender:humains|hommes}} et des anges, mais que je n’ai pas l’amour, je suis devenu un bronze qui fait écho ou une cymbale qui claque.
fr.B: Supposons que je parle les langues des {{gender:humains|hommes}}, et aussi celles des anges. Si je n’ai pas l’amour, je ne suis rien de plus qu’un bronze sonore ou une cymbale bruyante.
fr.R: Je pourrais peut-être parler en langues, dans les langues des gens et même dans celles des anges. Mais si je n’ai pas l’amour, je ne suis qu’un bruit vide, comme du métal qu’on frappe ou une cymbale qui fait du vacarme.

es.L: Si hablo en las lenguas de los {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}} y de los ángeles, pero no tengo amor, he llegado a ser bronce que retumba o címbalo que hace estruendo.
es.B: Supongamos que hablo en las lenguas de los {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}}, y también en las de los ángeles. Si no tengo amor, no soy más que un bronce que retumba o un címbalo estridente.
es.R: Quizás pueda hablar en lenguas, en los idiomas de la gente y hasta de los ángeles. Pero si no tengo amor, solo soy ruido vacío, como un metal que golpea o un platillo que estalla.

sw.L: Nikinena katika lugha za binadamu na za malaika pia, lakini sina upendo, nimekuwa shaba inayorindima au toazi linalogonga kelele.
sw.B: Tuseme ninanena kwa lugha za binadamu, na za malaika pia. Ikiwa sina upendo, mimi si kitu zaidi ya shaba inayorindima au toazi linalovuma kwa kishindo.
sw.R: Huenda nikaweza kunena kwa lugha, yaani lugha za watu na hata za malaika. Lakini kama sina upendo, mimi ni kelele tupu tu, kama chuma kinachogongwa au toazi linalolia kwa nguvu.

vi.L: Nếu tôi nói các thứ tiếng của loài người và của thiên sứ, nhưng không có tình yêu thương, thì tôi đã trở thành đồng vang tiếng hay chập chõa khua inh ỏi.
vi.B: Giả sử tôi nói được các thứ tiếng của loài người, và cả của thiên sứ nữa. Nếu tôi không có tình yêu thương, tôi chẳng khác gì tiếng đồng vang rền hay tiếng chập chõa chát chúa.
vi.R: Có thể tôi nói được tiếng lạ, nói được ngôn ngữ của loài người và ngay cả của thiên sứ. Nhưng nếu tôi không có tình yêu thương, tôi chỉ là một thứ tiếng ồn trống rỗng, như tiếng kim loại khua loảng xoảng hay tiếng chập chõa va vào nhau.

ko.L: 내가 사람들의 방언과 천사들의 [방언]으로 말하더라도 사랑이 없으면, 나는 울려 퍼지는 청동이나 요란하게 부딪치는 심벌즈가 된 것입니다.
ko.B: 내가 사람들의 방언으로, 또 천사들의 방언으로까지 말한다고 합시다. 그래도 사랑이 없다면, 나는 쿵쿵 울리는 청동이나 쨍쨍 부딪치는 심벌즈일 뿐입니다.
ko.R: 내가 방언으로 말할 수 있어서, 사람들의 말뿐 아니라 천사들의 말까지 한다고 합시다. 그러나 사랑이 없다면, 나는 시끄럽게 두드리는 쇠붙이나 요란한 심벌즈처럼 아무 뜻 없는 소리일 뿐입니다.

pt.L: Se eu falar nas línguas dos {{gender:seres humanos|homens}} e dos anjos, mas não tiver amor, eu me tornei um bronze que ecoa ou um címbalo estridente.
pt.B: Suponham que eu fale as línguas dos {{gender:seres humanos|homens}} e também as dos anjos. Se eu não tiver amor, não passo de um bronze que retumba ou de um címbalo que estrondeia.
pt.R: Talvez eu consiga falar em línguas, nos idiomas das pessoas e até nos dos anjos. Mas, se eu não tiver amor, sou só um barulho vazio, como metal batendo em metal ou um prato que estrondeia.

decisions.choice: tongues of human beings and of angels: the gift of tongues of 12:10, pictured at its very highest, speech in any human language and even in the language of angels
alternatives: eloquence in many human languages, with no reference to the gift
decisions.reason: Chapter 13 continues from 12:31 and takes up the gifts just listed, starting with the one the Corinthians prized most (14:1-25). γλώσσαις means both the tongue and a language. Some Jewish writings of the time speak of angels having their own language (the Testament of Job describes Job's daughters speaking in it), and some in Corinth may have thought their tongues were the speech of angels. Paul names the highest gift he can imagine in order to say that even this is nothing without love.

decisions.choice: if I speak: a supposed case, with Paul using himself as the example
decisions.reason: Ἐὰν with the subjunctive sets up a supposition, not a claim. In verses 1-3 Paul puts himself in the place of the most gifted person imaginable, so that no reader can think the rule applies only to others. He does speak in tongues (14:18), but the point is the supposition, not his experience.

decisions.choice: love: the self-giving care for others that God shows, which seeks their good rather than one's own
decisions.reason: ἀγάπην is the word Paul uses for God's love in Christ (Romans 5:8; 2 Corinthians 5:14) and for the love believers owe one another (8:1). Verses 4-7 describe it by what it does and does not do. It is not a feeling or a gift alongside the others but the way every gift is to be used (12:31; 14:1).

decisions.choice: echoing bronze and a clanging cymbal: loud metal instruments or objects that make noise without meaning
alternatives: a sounding jar in a theater
decisions.reason: χαλκὸς is bronze, and ἠχῶν means sounding or echoing; the phrase may describe a bronze gong, bronze instruments in general, or the bronze vessels said to have been set in theaters to carry the sound. Corinth was famous in the ancient world for its bronze. κύμβαλον is a cymbal, and ἀλαλάζον is used of loud wailing or crying out. Cymbals and gongs were played in the worship of pagan gods such as Cybele and Dionysus, which the Corinthians knew. The point is that speech without love is noise, however impressive.

decisions.choice: I have become: the perfect tense describes the state that results; I am now nothing but noise
decisions.reason: γέγονα is a perfect. It does not describe a change at some past moment but what the speaker is: if the condition is met, that is what he has turned into.

decisions.choice: love (L, B, R), here and throughout the chapter
decisions.reason: The King James Version says "charity" in this chapter, following the Latin word caritas. In modern English "charity" means giving to the poor or an organization that does so, which verse 3 shows is not what Paul means. "Love" is used at every level.

decisions.choice: {{gender:human beings|men}}
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων here means people in general, set against angels, so the inclusive form is the default and "men" the alternative.

decisions.choice: speak in tongues, in the languages of people (R); I am only empty noise, like banging metal or a crashing cymbal (R)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the name of the gift, "tongues", and adds "languages" to explain it (m1). It says what the picture means, empty noise (m4), and uses "banging metal" because a bronze object would be unfamiliar.

decisions.choice: l’amour, here and throughout the chapter
decisions.reason: Older French Bibles say "la charité" here, after the Latin caritas. In modern French "charité" means giving to the poor, which verse 3 shows is not what Paul means (m3); "amour" is the ordinary word, as the English says "love".

decisions.choice: amor
decisions.reason: As the English keeps "love", Spanish says "amor" at every level through the chapter; "caridad", the older rendering, now means giving to the poor.

decisions.choice: {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}}
decisions.reason: Spanish follows the English setting, as in 2:3: the word means human beings of either sex.

decisions.choice: hablar en lenguas, en los idiomas de la gente
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "lenguas", the name of the gift in 12:10, and adds "idiomas" as the English adds "languages", so the reader sees the gift at its highest (m1).

decisions.choice: upendo
decisions.reason: "Upendo" for agape at every level through the chapter, the word used for it throughout the letters; "mapenzi" suggests romantic love or will.

decisions.choice: binadamu: no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: "Binadamu" already means human beings of both sexes, so the English gender span has nothing to change; "lugha" for tongues as in 12:10.

decisions.choice: toazi
decisions.reason: "Toazi" is the Swahili word for a pair of clashing cymbals; "upatu" is a gong-like metal plate.

decisions.choice: "tình yêu thương" for agape at every level through chapter 13, never "lòng bác ái"
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice: "love", never "charity". "Tình yêu thương" is the word of the Vietnamese Colossians and Thessalonians for agape; "lòng bác ái" means charity to the poor, and "tình yêu" alone suggests romantic love. The same word is kept in every verse of the chapter, as the Greek keeps one word.

decisions.choice: "các thứ tiếng" (L, B); "tiếng lạ ... ngôn ngữ" (R) for the tongues of human beings and angels
decisions.reason: Here the gift of 12:10 is pictured at its height as speech in any language (m1), so Literal and Balanced say "thứ tiếng"; Readable names the gift and the languages, as the English does. "Loài người" needs no gender span.

decisions.choice: "사랑" at every level, the one word for love through the chapter and the letter
decisions.reason: The project's choice is "love", never "charity"; Korean "사랑" is the word of 8:1 and Romans for God's love and the love believers owe one another.

decisions.choice: "방언" (L, B), "말" (R) for the tongues of people and angels; "청동", "심벌즈"
decisions.reason: The verse takes up the gift of 12:10, so Literal and Balanced keep "방언"; the meaning decision footnotes "languages", which Readable says, as the English does. "꽹과리" is a Korean folk instrument and would bring in a picture the Greek does not have; "심벌즈" names the instrument.

decisions.choice: amor, here and throughout the chapter
decisions.reason: "Amor" at every level, never "caridade", which older Catholic Portuguese Bibles used here after the Latin; in Brazil today "caridade" means alms or charitable work, which verse 3 shows is not the point (m3).

decisions.choice: falar em línguas, nos idiomas das pessoas; um prato que estrondeia
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the gift's name "línguas" and adds "idiomas", as the English adds "languages" (m1). "Prato" is the everyday Brazilian word for a cymbal; Literal and Balanced keep "címbalo", the instrument's proper name.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ἔχω προφητείαν καὶ εἰδῶ τὰ μυστήρια πάντα καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γνῶσιν, καὶ ἐὰν ἔχω πᾶσαν τὴν πίστιν ὥστε ὄρη μεθιστάναι, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, οὐθέν εἰμι.

records.literal_gloss: And if I have prophecy and know the mysteries all and all the knowledge, and if I have all the faith so as mountains to move, love but not I have, nothing I am.

en.L: And if I have prophecy and know all the mysteries and all the knowledge, and if I have all the faith, so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.
en.B: I may be able to prophesy, and know every mystery and everything there is to know; I may have all the faith there is, enough to move mountains; but if I do not have love, I am nothing.
en.R: I might be able to prophesy. I might understand every mystery of God and know everything there is to know. I might have so much faith that I could tell mountains to move, and they would move. But if I do not have love, I am nothing.

fr.L: Et si j’ai la prophétie, et que je connais tous les mystères et toute la connaissance, et si j’ai toute la foi, au point de déplacer des montagnes, mais que je n’ai pas l’amour, je ne suis rien.
fr.B: Je pourrais prophétiser, connaître tous les mystères et tout ce qu’il y a à savoir ; je pourrais avoir toute la foi possible, assez pour déplacer des montagnes ; mais si je n’ai pas l’amour, je ne suis rien.
fr.R: Je pourrais peut-être prophétiser. Je pourrais comprendre tous les mystères de Dieu et savoir tout ce qu’il y a à savoir. Je pourrais avoir tellement de foi que je dirais aux montagnes de bouger, et elles bougeraient. Mais si je n’ai pas l’amour, je ne suis rien.

es.L: Y si tengo profecía y conozco todos los misterios y todo el conocimiento, y si tengo toda la fe, de modo que traslade montañas, pero no tengo amor, nada soy.
es.B: Puede que tenga el don de profecía, y que conozca todos los misterios y todo lo que se puede saber; puede que tenga toda la fe que existe, tanta que mueva montañas; pero si no tengo amor, no soy nada.
es.R: Quizás pueda profetizar. Quizás entienda todos los misterios de Dios y sepa todo lo que se puede saber. Quizás tenga tanta fe que pueda decirles a las montañas que se muevan, y se muevan. Pero si no tengo amor, no soy nada.

sw.L: Na ikiwa ninao unabii, na ninaelewa siri zote na kila maarifa, na ikiwa ninayo imani yote hata niweze kuhamisha milima, lakini sina upendo, mimi si kitu.
sw.B: Huenda nikaweza kutoa unabii, na kuelewa kila siri na kila kitu kinachoweza kujulikana; huenda nikawa na imani yote iliyopo, ya kutosha kuhamisha milima; lakini ikiwa sina upendo, mimi si kitu.
sw.R: Huenda nikaweza kutoa unabii. Huenda nikaelewa kila siri ya Mungu na kujua kila kitu kinachoweza kujulikana. Huenda nikawa na imani kubwa kiasi kwamba ningeiambia milima ihame, nayo ingehama. Lakini kama sina upendo, mimi si kitu.

vi.L: Và nếu tôi có lời tiên tri và biết mọi sự mầu nhiệm và mọi tri thức, và nếu tôi có trọn đức tin đến nỗi dời núi được, nhưng không có tình yêu thương, thì tôi chẳng là gì cả.
vi.B: Có thể tôi nói tiên tri được, biết mọi sự mầu nhiệm và mọi điều cần biết; có thể tôi có tất cả đức tin, đủ để dời núi; nhưng nếu tôi không có tình yêu thương, tôi chẳng là gì cả.
vi.R: Có thể tôi nói tiên tri được. Có thể tôi hiểu được mọi sự mầu nhiệm của Đức Chúa Trời và biết mọi điều có thể biết. Có thể tôi có đức tin lớn đến nỗi tôi bảo núi dời đi và núi dời đi. Nhưng nếu tôi không có tình yêu thương, tôi chẳng là gì cả.

ko.L: 내가 예언을 가지고 있고 모든 비밀과 모든 지식을 알고, 또 산을 옮길 만한 모든 믿음을 가지고 있더라도 사랑이 없으면, 나는 아무것도 아닙니다.
ko.B: 내가 예언을 할 수 있고, 모든 비밀과 알 수 있는 모든 것을 안다고 합시다. 산을 옮길 만큼 온전한 믿음을 가지고 있다고 합시다. 그래도 사랑이 없다면, 나는 아무것도 아닙니다.
ko.R: 내가 예언을 할 수 있다고 합시다. 하나님의 모든 비밀을 깨닫고, 알아야 할 모든 것을 안다고 합시다. 또 산더러 움직이라고 하면 산이 움직일 만큼 큰 믿음이 있다고 합시다. 그래도 사랑이 없다면, 나는 아무것도 아닙니다.

pt.L: E, se eu tiver profecia e souber todos os mistérios e todo o conhecimento, e se eu tiver toda a fé, de modo a mover montanhas, mas não tiver amor, nada sou.
pt.B: Posso ser capaz de profetizar e conhecer todos os mistérios e tudo o que se pode saber; posso ter toda a fé que existe, a ponto de mover montanhas; mas, se eu não tiver amor, não sou nada.
pt.R: Talvez eu consiga profetizar. Talvez eu entenda todos os mistérios de Deus e saiba tudo o que se pode saber. Talvez eu tenha tanta fé que poderia mandar as montanhas saírem do lugar, e elas sairiam. Mas, se eu não tiver amor, não sou nada.

decisions.choice: have prophecy: have the gift of prophecy, speaking a message from God for the church
decisions.reason: προφητείαν is the gift of 12:10 and 12:28, the one Paul ranks highest in chapter 14 because it builds up the church (14:1-5). To "have" it is to have been given the gift.

decisions.choice: know all the mysteries and all knowledge: understand every part of God's hidden purposes and all that can be known of them
decisions.reason: μυστήρια are God's purposes once hidden and now revealed (2:1, 7; 4:1; 15:51). γνῶσιν is the gift of 12:8, prized in Corinth (8:1). "All" is said twice: Paul imagines the gift with no limit at all.

decisions.choice: all faith: the special gift of faith of 12:9, confidence that God will act, at its fullest
decisions.reason: Every believer has faith in Christ, but here πίστιν is the gift given only to some (12:9), and πᾶσαν pictures it with nothing lacking. The key term "faith" is kept.

decisions.choice: so as to move mountains: an echo of Jesus' saying about faith that can move a mountain
decisions.reason: Jesus said that faith could tell a mountain to be lifted up and thrown into the sea (Mark 11:23; Matthew 17:20; 21:21). Paul uses the saying to describe faith that can do what seems impossible.

decisions.choice: I am nothing: worth nothing in God's sight, not merely without benefit
decisions.reason: οὐθέν εἰμι is stronger than verse 3, "I gain nothing". The person with the greatest gifts but no love does not just lose something; in what counts before God, he is nothing (compare 3:7, where Paul says that the planter and waterer are nothing).

decisions.choice: I may be able to prophesy (B); I might be able to prophesy (R)
alternatives: I may have the gift of prophecy
decisions.reason: "Have prophecy" is not natural English. Balanced and Readable say it with the verb; the gift is the same (m1).

decisions.choice: every mystery of God; I could tell mountains to move, and they would move
decisions.reason: Readable says whose mysteries they are (m2) and spells out the saying of Jesus behind the picture (m4). "Mystery" is the settled key term and is kept.

decisions.choice: siri; maarifa
decisions.reason: "Siri" for mysterion as in 2:7, and "maarifa" for gnosis as in chapter 8 and the gift of 12:8.

decisions.choice: the supposed case as "... 한다고 합시다" (B, R), then "그래도 사랑이 없다면"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break Paul's long conditions into short suppositions, as the English does, so the repeated "but if I do not have love" stands out in each of verses 1-3.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ψωμίσω πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντά μου, καὶ ἐὰν παραδῶ τὸ σῶμά μου, ἵνα καυθήσομαι, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, οὐδὲν ὠφελοῦμαι.

records.literal_gloss: And if I give away in food all the possessions of me, and if I hand over the body of me so that I will be burned, love but not I have, nothing I am benefited.

en.L: And if I give away all my possessions as food, and if I hand over my body so that I will be burned, but do not have love, I am benefited nothing.
en.B: I may hand out everything I own as food for others; I may hand over my body to the flames; but if I do not have love, it does me no good at all.
en.R: I might give away everything I own to feed hungry people. I might even give up my life and let them burn my body. But if I do not have love, it does me no good.

fr.L: Et si je distribue en nourriture tous mes biens, et si je livre mon corps pour que je sois brûlé, mais que je n’ai pas l’amour, je n’en tire aucun profit.
fr.B: Je pourrais distribuer tout ce que je possède pour nourrir les autres ; je pourrais livrer mon corps aux flammes ; mais si je n’ai pas l’amour, cela ne me sert absolument à rien.
fr.R: Je pourrais donner tout ce que j’ai pour nourrir ceux qui ont faim. Je pourrais même donner ma vie et accepter qu’on brûle mon corps. Mais si je n’ai pas l’amour, cela ne me sert à rien.

es.L: Y si reparto todos mis bienes como alimento, y si entrego mi cuerpo para ser quemado, pero no tengo amor, de nada me aprovecha.
es.B: Puedo repartir todo lo que tengo para dar de comer a otros; puedo entregar mi cuerpo a las llamas; pero si no tengo amor, de nada me sirve.
es.R: Quizás regale todo lo que tengo para alimentar a los que tienen hambre. Quizás hasta dé mi vida y deje que quemen mi cuerpo. Pero si no tengo amor, eso no me sirve de nada.

sw.L: Na nikigawa mali zangu zote kidogo kidogo kuwa chakula, na nikiukabidhi mwili wangu ili nichomwe moto, lakini sina upendo, sipati faida yoyote.
sw.B: Huenda nikagawa kila kitu nilicho nacho kuwa chakula cha wengine; huenda nikaukabidhi mwili wangu kwa moto; lakini kama sina upendo, hilo halinisaidii chochote.
sw.R: Huenda nikatoa kila kitu nilicho nacho ili kuwalisha watu wenye njaa. Huenda hata nikayatoa maisha yangu, nikawaacha wauchome mwili wangu. Lakini kama sina upendo, hilo halinisaidii kitu.

vi.L: Và nếu tôi đem hết của cải mình mà phân phát làm thức ăn, và nếu tôi phó thân thể mình để bị thiêu đốt, nhưng không có tình yêu thương, thì tôi chẳng được ích lợi gì.
vi.B: Có thể tôi đem hết mọi thứ mình có ra phân phát làm thức ăn cho người khác; có thể tôi phó thân thể mình cho lửa thiêu; nhưng nếu tôi không có tình yêu thương, điều đó chẳng ích lợi gì cho tôi cả.
vi.R: Có thể tôi đem cho hết mọi thứ mình có để nuôi những người đói. Có thể tôi còn hy sinh mạng sống mình và để người ta thiêu đốt thân thể tôi. Nhưng nếu tôi không có tình yêu thương, điều đó chẳng giúp ích gì cho tôi.

ko.L: 내가 내 모든 소유를 [남에게] 먹을 것으로 나누어 주고, 또 내 몸을 넘겨주어 불에 타게 하더라도 사랑이 없으면, 나에게는 아무 유익이 없습니다.
ko.B: 내가 가진 모든 것을 다른 사람들의 먹을 것으로 나누어 준다고 합시다. 내 몸을 불길에 내어 준다고 합시다. 그래도 사랑이 없다면, 나에게는 아무런 유익이 없습니다.
ko.R: 내가 가진 모든 것을 배고픈 사람들을 먹이는 데 다 내준다고 합시다. 내가 목숨까지 내놓아서 사람들이 내 몸을 불태우게 한다고 합시다. 그래도 사랑이 없다면, 그것은 나에게 아무 도움이 되지 않습니다.

pt.L: E, se eu repartir como alimento todos os meus bens, e se eu entregar o meu corpo para que eu seja queimado, mas não tiver amor, em nada sou beneficiado.
pt.B: Posso distribuir tudo o que tenho como alimento para os outros; posso entregar o meu corpo às chamas; mas, se eu não tiver amor, isso não me serve de nada.
pt.R: Talvez eu dê tudo o que tenho para alimentar quem passa fome. Talvez eu até entregue a minha vida e deixe que queimem o meu corpo. Mas, se eu não tiver amor, isso não me adianta nada.

decisions.choice: so that I will be burned, as the SBLGNT reads; manuscripts are divided between this and "so that I may boast"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads καυθήσομαι, "I will be burned". From general knowledge: several of the oldest manuscripts, including the early papyrus P46 and the codices Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus, read a word that differs by one letter, "so that I may boast"; many later manuscripts and early translations read forms of "be burned". "Boast" is the harder reading and would mean giving up one's body to win a reason for pride; Paul elsewhere speaks of boasting in a good sense (9:15-16). "Be burned" fits the climax of the list and was understood this way by many early writers, but its odd grammar may show it is a correction. Reviewers must check the SBLGNT apparatus before this sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: give away all my possessions as food: hand out everything one owns, bit by bit, to feed others
decisions.reason: ψωμίσω means to feed, especially by giving out food in small portions. Paul pictures someone who gives away every last thing to feed the poor, the greatest act of generosity he can name.

decisions.choice: hand over my body to be burned: give up one's life by fire, as a martyr
alternatives: sell oneself into slavery to help others
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls the three young men in Daniel 3, who gave up their bodies to the fire rather than worship an idol (Daniel 3:28), a story Jews of Paul's day told of those faithful to death. Some have thought instead of selling oneself as a slave, whose body was branded; that suits the reading "so that I may boast" better (m1).

decisions.choice: I gain nothing: it brings me no benefit before God
decisions.reason: ὠφελοῦμαι is passive, "I am benefited". The others may be helped by the gifts and the sacrifice, but the giver without love gains nothing from them on the day God judges (3:13-15; 4:5).

decisions.choice: hand over my body to the flames (B); give up my life and let them burn my body (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the SBLGNT reading (m1) and say plainly that the person dies by fire (m3); the footnote gives "so that I may boast".

decisions.choice: to feed hungry people
decisions.reason: Readable says who is fed (m2).

decisions.choice: nikiukabidhi mwili wangu
decisions.reason: "Kukabidhi", the verb used for paradidomi in 11:2 and 11:23, for handing over the body to death.

decisions.choice: "để bị thiêu đốt" (L), "cho lửa thiêu" (B), "để người ta thiêu đốt" (R), following the SBLGNT, with "để tôi được khoe mình" (so that I may boast) footnoted
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "so that I will be burned"; manuscripts are divided (m1), and the footnote gives the other reading in the word of 1:29-31.

decisions.choice: "불에 타게 하다" (L); "불길에 내어 주다" (B); "불태우게 하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "so that I will be burned"; the manuscripts are divided, and the meaning decision footnotes "so that I may boast".

source.text: Ἡ ἀγάπη μακροθυμεῖ, χρηστεύεται ἡ ἀγάπη, οὐ ζηλοῖ ἡ ἀγάπη, οὐ περπερεύεται, οὐ φυσιοῦται, οὐκ ἀσχημονεῖ, οὐ ζητεῖ τὰ ἑαυτῆς, οὐ παροξύνεται, οὐ λογίζεται τὸ κακόν, οὐ χαίρει ἐπὶ τῇ ἀδικίᾳ, συγχαίρει δὲ τῇ ἀληθείᾳ·

records.literal_gloss: The love is patient, is kind the love, not envies the love, not brags, not is puffed up, \v 5 not behaves improperly, not seeks the [things] of itself, not is provoked, not reckons the evil, \v 6 not rejoices over the unrighteousness, rejoices with but the truth;

en.L: Love is patient, love is kind, love does not envy, does not brag, is not puffed up, \v 5 does not behave improperly, does not seek its own [things], is not provoked, does not reckon the wrong, \v 6 does not rejoice over unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth.
en.B: Love is patient; love is kind. Love does not envy, does not show off, is not puffed up. \v 5 It does not behave shamefully, it does not look for its own advantage, it does not lose its temper, and it does not keep a tally of wrongs. \v 6 It takes no pleasure in wrongdoing, but shares the joy of the truth.
en.R: Love is patient with others and kind to them. Love does not envy others. It does not brag, and it does not act proud. \v 5 It does not treat people rudely. It does not put itself first. It does not lose its temper. It does not keep thinking about the wrongs others have done to it. \v 6 It is not happy about wrongdoing, but it is glad about what is true.

fr.L: L’amour est patient, l’amour agit avec bonté, l’amour n’envie pas, ne fanfaronne pas, ne se gonfle pas, \v 5 ne se conduit pas de façon inconvenante, ne cherche pas ce qui est à lui, ne s’irrite pas, ne compte pas le mal, \v 6 ne se réjouit pas de l’injustice, mais se réjouit avec la vérité.
fr.B: L’amour est patient ; l’amour agit avec bonté. L’amour n’envie pas, ne cherche pas à briller, ne se gonfle pas d’orgueil. \v 5 Il ne fait rien de honteux, il ne cherche pas son propre intérêt, il ne se met pas en colère, et il ne tient pas le compte des torts. \v 6 Il ne prend aucun plaisir au mal, mais il partage la joie de la vérité.
fr.R: L’amour est patient avec les autres et bon envers eux. L’amour n’envie pas les autres. Il ne cherche pas à se faire remarquer, et il n’est pas orgueilleux. \v 5 Il ne traite pas les gens avec grossièreté. Il ne se met pas à la première place. Il ne se met pas en colère. Il ne repense pas sans cesse au mal que les autres lui ont fait. \v 6 Il n’est pas content quand on fait le mal, mais il est heureux de ce qui est vrai.

es.L: El amor es paciente, el amor es bondadoso; el amor no envidia, no presume, no se envanece, \v 5 no se comporta indecorosamente, no busca lo suyo, no se irrita, no toma en cuenta el mal, \v 6 no se alegra de la injusticia, sino que se alegra con la verdad;
es.B: El amor es paciente; el amor es bondadoso. El amor no envidia, no hace alarde, no se envanece. \v 5 No actúa de forma vergonzosa, no busca su propio provecho, no pierde los estribos y no lleva la cuenta de las ofensas. \v 6 No se alegra del mal que se hace, sino que comparte la alegría de la verdad.
es.R: El amor es paciente y bondadoso con los demás. El amor no tiene envidia de nadie. No presume, ni actúa con orgullo. \v 5 No trata a la gente con grosería. No se pone a sí mismo en primer lugar. No pierde la paciencia. No se queda pensando en el mal que otros le han hecho. \v 6 No se alegra cuando se hace el mal, sino que se alegra con lo que es verdad.

sw.L: Upendo huvumilia kwa subira, upendo hutenda wema, upendo hauoni wivu, haujisifu, hauvimbi kwa kiburi, \v 5 hautendi mambo ya aibu, hautafuti faida yake wenyewe, hauchokozeki, hauweki hesabu ya ubaya, \v 6 haushangilii yasiyo ya haki, lakini hushangilia pamoja na kweli.
sw.B: Upendo una subira; upendo una wema. Upendo hauna wivu, haujionyeshi, hauvimbi kwa kiburi. \v 5 Hautendi mambo ya aibu, hautafuti faida yake wenyewe, haupandwi na hasira, wala hauweki hesabu ya makosa. \v 6 Hauoni raha katika maovu, bali hushiriki furaha ya kweli.
sw.R: Upendo huwavumilia wengine na huwatendea wema. Upendo hauwaonei wengine wivu. Haujisifu, wala hauna kiburi. \v 5 Hauwatendei watu kwa ufidhuli. Haujitangulizi wenyewe. Haupandwi na hasira. Haukai ukiwaza mabaya ambayo wengine wameutendea. \v 6 Haufurahii maovu, bali hufurahia yaliyo kweli.

vi.L: Tình yêu thương thì kiên nhẫn, tình yêu thương thì tử tế, tình yêu thương không ganh tị, không khoe khoang, không kiêu căng, \v 5 không cư xử khiếm nhã, không tìm điều thuộc về mình, không bị kích động, không ghi nhớ điều ác, \v 6 không vui về sự bất chính, nhưng cùng vui với chân lý.
vi.B: Tình yêu thương thì nhẫn nại; tình yêu thương thì nhân hậu. Tình yêu thương không ganh tị, không phô trương, không kiêu căng. \v 5 Tình yêu thương không làm điều đáng hổ thẹn, không tìm lợi ích cho riêng mình, không nổi nóng, và không ghi sổ những điều sai trái. \v 6 Tình yêu thương không thích thú điều bất chính, nhưng chia vui với chân lý.
vi.R: Tình yêu thương kiên nhẫn với người khác và tử tế với họ. Tình yêu thương không ganh tị với ai. Tình yêu thương không khoe khoang, cũng không tỏ ra kiêu ngạo. \v 5 Tình yêu thương không cư xử thô lỗ với người ta. Tình yêu thương không đặt mình lên trước. Tình yêu thương không nổi nóng. Tình yêu thương không cứ nghĩ mãi về những điều sai trái người khác đã làm cho mình. \v 6 Tình yêu thương không vui khi thấy điều sai trái, nhưng vui về những gì là thật.

ko.L: 사랑은 참을성이 많고, 사랑은 친절합니다. 사랑은 시샘하지 않습니다. [사랑은] 허풍을 떨지 않고, 우쭐하지 않으며, \v 5 체면 없이 행동하지 않고, 자기 것을 구하지 않고, 화를 내지 않고, 악을 셈하지 않으며, \v 6 불의를 기뻐하지 않고 진리와 함께 기뻐합니다.
ko.B: 사랑은 끈기 있게 참아 주고, 사랑은 친절합니다. 사랑은 남을 시샘하지 않고, 자기를 내세우지 않으며, 우쭐하지 않습니다. \v 5 사랑은 부끄러운 짓을 하지 않고, 자기 유익을 찾지 않으며, 쉽게 화를 내지 않고, 남이 저지른 잘못을 장부에 적어 두지 않습니다. \v 6 사랑은 옳지 않은 일을 즐거워하지 않고, 진리가 이길 때 함께 기뻐합니다.
ko.R: 사랑은 다른 사람을 끈기 있게 참아 주고 친절하게 대합니다. 사랑은 남을 시샘하지 않습니다. 사랑은 잘난 척하지 않고, 교만하게 굴지 않습니다. \v 5 사랑은 사람들을 무시하며 함부로 대하지 않습니다. 자기를 앞세우지 않습니다. 쉽게 화내지 않습니다. 다른 사람이 자기에게 한 잘못을 계속 마음에 담아 두지 않습니다. \v 6 사랑은 나쁜 일을 보고 기뻐하지 않고, 참된 것을 보고 기뻐합니다.

pt.L: O amor tem paciência, o amor age com bondade, o amor não tem inveja, não se exibe, não se incha, \v 5 não se porta de modo indecoroso, não busca as [coisas] próprias, não se irrita, não leva em conta o mal, \v 6 não se alegra com a injustiça, mas se alegra junto com a verdade.
pt.B: O amor tem paciência; o amor é bondoso. O amor não tem inveja, não se exibe, não fica cheio de si. \v 5 Não se comporta de modo vergonhoso, não procura a própria vantagem, não perde a calma e não mantém registro das ofensas. \v 6 Não tem prazer na injustiça, mas participa da alegria da verdade.
pt.R: O amor tem paciência com os outros e é bondoso com eles. O amor não tem inveja dos outros. Ele não se gaba e não age com orgulho. \v 5 Não trata as pessoas com grosseria. Não se coloca em primeiro lugar. Não perde a calma. Não fica lembrando o mal que os outros fizeram contra ele. \v 6 Não fica contente com o que é errado, mas se alegra com o que é verdadeiro.

decisions.choice: love is described by verbs: what it does and what it does not do
decisions.reason: Paul does not define love; in verses 4-7 he describes it with fifteen verbs, as if it were a person. Most of the verbs are negative, and several name faults Paul has already rebuked in Corinth: jealousy (3:3), being puffed up (4:6, 18-19; 5:2; 8:1), seeking one's own advantage (10:24, 33) and behaving shamefully at the Lord's Supper (11:20-22). The portrait is also a portrait of Christ, who did all these things for others.

decisions.choice: patient, kind: slow to anger with others, and active in doing them good
decisions.reason: μακροθυμεῖ means to bear long with others and not strike back; χρηστεύεται is to show kindness, to be generous and useful to others. Paul joins God's patience and kindness in Romans 2:4, and lists the two side by side as fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22).

decisions.choice: does not envy, does not brag, is not puffed up: free of rivalry and self-display
decisions.reason: ζηλοῖ is the verb of 12:31 and 14:1, used here in its bad sense, to envy, as its noun is in 3:3. περπερεύεται occurs only here in the New Testament and means to talk oneself up, to show off. φυσιοῦται is the verb for being puffed up that Paul uses through the letter (4:6; 8:1).

decisions.choice: does not behave shamefully, does not seek its own: does not act in ways that disgrace itself or others, and does not pursue its own advantage
decisions.reason: ἀσχημονεῖ is to behave improperly or disgracefully (7:36; compare 12:23). ζητεῖ τὰ ἑαυτῆς repeats Paul's rule in 10:24 and 10:33: seek the good of others, not your own.

decisions.choice: is not provoked: does not become angry or irritated
decisions.reason: παροξύνεται is to be stirred to anger (Acts 17:16). Love does not let other people's faults make it bitter.

decisions.choice: does not keep account of wrongs: does not count up the wrong done to it or hold it against the one who did it
alternatives: does not plot evil, does not plan harm to others
decisions.reason: λογίζεται is a word for reckoning and keeping accounts; Paul uses it in 2 Corinthians 5:19 for God "not counting their trespasses against them". On this reading love keeps no record of wrongs suffered. The same words can also mean to plan harm: Zechariah 8:17 in the Greek Old Testament tells Israel not to devise evil against a neighbor in their hearts. Both readings fit; the accounting sense matches the verbs of patience around it.

decisions.choice: rejoices with the truth: shares in the joy when the truth prevails, as if truth were a person
decisions.reason: ἀδικίᾳ (wrongdoing, injustice) and ἀληθείᾳ are set against each other, as in Romans 2:8. Truth here is not only accurate statements but what is right and true, including the truth of the gospel. συγχαίρει means to rejoice together with someone; love and truth are glad together.

decisions.choice: the list is kept as verbs: love is patient, love is kind, does not envy, does not brag
decisions.reason: The Greek uses verbs, not adjectives, so each level says what love does. The opening words, "love is patient, love is kind", are what the Greek says and cannot be put more simply; they are kept although they are familiar. Readable spells out the objects ("with others", "to them").

decisions.choice: does not brag (L, R), does not show off (B); puffed up (L, B), proud (R)
decisions.reason: "Boast" is kept for a different word family in this letter (1:29-31; 13:3 footnote), so this rare verb is "brag" or "show off". The verb for being puffed up has the settled wording for 1 Corinthians.

decisions.choice: does not behave shamefully (B), does not treat people rudely (R); does not lose its temper (B, R)
decisions.reason: Plain words for improper behavior (m4) and for being provoked to anger (m5). "Easily" is not added; the Greek says love is not provoked at all.

decisions.choice: does not reckon the wrong (L); does not keep a tally of wrongs (B); does not keep thinking about the wrongs others have done to it (R)
decisions.reason: Each level gives the accounting sense chosen in m6; the footnote gives "does not plot evil".

decisions.choice: shares the joy of the truth (B); is glad about what is true (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of rejoicing together (m7); Readable says it simply.

decisions.choice: l’amour est patient, l’amour agit avec bonté: the list kept as verbs at every level
decisions.reason: As in English, the Greek describes love by what it does (m1), so French uses a verb for the second item too ("agit avec bonté") rather than an adjective. Balanced and Readable then refer to love as "il", the French pronoun for "amour".

decisions.choice: ne fanfaronne pas (L), ne cherche pas à briller (B), ne cherche pas à se faire remarquer (R); ne se gonfle pas (L), ne se gonfle pas d’orgueil (B), n’est pas orgueilleux (R)
decisions.reason: "Se vanter" is kept for the boasting word family of the letter (1:29-31; 13:3 footnote), as the English keeps "boast", so this rarer verb is rendered by words for showing off. The verb for being puffed up follows the wording the French of chapter 8 uses ("gonfle", "gonfle d’orgueil", "orgueilleux").

decisions.choice: no presume (L, R), no hace alarde (B); no se envanece (L, B), no actúa con orgullo (R)
decisions.reason: "Envanecerse" is the word kept for this verb since 4:6, with pride at Readable. "Presumir" is the Readable word for bragging in 3:21 and 4:7; Balanced says "hacer alarde", as the English says "show off".

decisions.choice: no toma en cuenta el mal (L); no lleva la cuenta de las ofensas (B); no se queda pensando en el mal que otros le han hecho (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is keeping account of wrongs done (m6, footnoted). Each level keeps the picture of counting; "no guarda rencor" would say a feeling, not the act.

decisions.choice: verbs and verb phrases throughout: huvumilia kwa subira, hutenda wema, hauoni wivu, haujisifu, hauvimbi kwa kiburi (L)
decisions.reason: As in English, love is described by what it does; Swahili verbs with the negative ha- carry the list naturally. "Hauvimbi kwa kiburi" (L, B) and "hauna kiburi" (R) are the settled words for physioo (4:6; 8:1).

decisions.choice: yasiyo ya haki (L); maovu (B, R)
decisions.reason: Adikia is the opposite of "haki" (righteousness), so Literal shows the link.

decisions.choice: the list as verbs with "tình yêu thương" as subject: "kiên nhẫn", "tử tế" (L), "nhẫn nại", "nhân hậu" (B); "không ganh tị", "không khoe khoang" (L, R), "không phô trương" (B); "không kiêu căng" (L, B), "không ... kiêu ngạo" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English does, the list stays a list of what love does and does not do (m1). The wording is drafted fresh: this chapter is among the best known in the 1926 version, whose old forms ("hay nhịn nhục", "chẳng") the style guide asks drafts not to drift toward. "Kiêu căng" is the word for physioo through the letter (4:6).

decisions.choice: "không ghi nhớ điều ác" (L); "không ghi sổ những điều sai trái" (B); "không cứ nghĩ mãi về những điều sai trái người khác đã làm cho mình" (R) for ou logizetai to kakon
decisions.reason: The verb is the bookkeeper's "reckon" (m6); Balanced keeps the picture of an account book, as the English "tally" does.

decisions.choice: love described by verbs at every level: "참을성이 많다, 친절하다, 시샘하지 않다, 허풍을 떨지 않다, 우쭐하지 않다, 체면 없이 행동하지 않다, 자기 것을 구하지 않다, 화를 내지 않다, 악을 셈하지 않다" (L)
decisions.reason: These verses are among the best known in Korean, and the older and current Korean Bibles fix their wording in readers' ears; drafted from the Greek, the words here are chosen to say what the meaning decisions describe in modern Korean without repeating those versions. "우쭐하다" is the word of 4:6 and 8:1 for being puffed up; "자기 것을 구하다" is the phrase of 10:24; "셈하다" keeps the bookkeeping word of the Greek that Balanced spells out as "장부에 적어 두다".

decisions.choice: "[사랑은]" (L) where the Greek drops the subject after three uses
decisions.reason: Korean needs a subject at the start of a new sentence; Balanced and Readable repeat "사랑은" without brackets.

decisions.choice: tem paciência (L, B, R); age com bondade (L), é bondoso (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek describes love with verbs (m1). "Tem paciência" keeps a verbal phrase at every level and Literal says "age com bondade" for the second verb; Balanced and Readable say "é bondoso", the plain Portuguese for showing kindness.

decisions.choice: não se exibe (L, B), não se gaba (R); não se incha (L), não fica cheio de si (B), não age com orgulho (R); não se porta de modo indecoroso (L)
decisions.reason: The rare verb for showing off is "exibir-se" or "gabar-se", leaving the "gloriar-se" / "orgulho" family to boasting (9:15). "Inchar-se" is the Literal picture of being puffed up; "cheio de si" is the living Portuguese idiom for it, and Readable says "orgulho", as the book's terms give "proud". Literal's "indecoroso" links the verb with the parts "indecorosos" of 12:23 (m4).

source.text: πάντα στέγει, πάντα πιστεύει, πάντα ἐλπίζει, πάντα ὑπομένει.

records.literal_gloss: All things it bears, all things it believes, all things it hopes, all things it endures.

en.L: All things it bears, all things it believes, all things it hopes, all things it endures.
en.B: There is nothing love cannot bear, no time when it stops believing or hoping, nothing it cannot endure.
en.R: Love puts up with anything. It keeps believing and keeps hoping, whatever happens. It keeps going through every trouble.

fr.L: Tout, il le supporte ; tout, il le croit ; tout, il l’espère ; tout, il l’endure.
fr.B: Il n’y a rien que l’amour ne puisse supporter ; jamais il ne cesse de croire ni d’espérer ; il n’y a rien qu’il ne puisse endurer.
fr.R: L’amour supporte n’importe quoi. Il continue à croire et à espérer, quoi qu’il arrive. Il tient bon dans toutes les difficultés.

es.L: Todo lo sobrelleva, todo lo cree, todo lo espera, todo lo resiste.
es.B: No hay nada que el amor no pueda sobrellevar; nunca deja de creer ni de esperar; no hay nada que no pueda resistir.
es.R: El amor aguanta cualquier cosa. Sigue creyendo y sigue esperando, pase lo que pase. Sigue adelante en medio de cualquier dificultad.

sw.L: Yote huyabeba, yote huyaamini, yote huyatumaini, yote huyastahimili.
sw.B: Hakuna jambo ambalo upendo hauwezi kulibeba, hakuna wakati unapoacha kuamini au kutumaini, hakuna jambo usiloweza kulistahimili.
sw.R: Upendo huvumilia lolote. Huendelea kuamini na kutumaini, liwalo na liwe. Huendelea mbele katika kila taabu.

vi.L: Mọi sự [tình yêu thương] đều gánh chịu, mọi sự đều tin, mọi sự đều hy vọng, mọi sự đều kiên trì.
vi.B: Không có điều gì tình yêu thương không thể gánh chịu, không lúc nào thôi tin tưởng hay hy vọng, không có điều gì không thể kiên trì chịu đựng.
vi.R: Tình yêu thương chịu đựng được mọi điều. Tình yêu thương cứ tin và cứ hy vọng, dù có chuyện gì xảy ra. Tình yêu thương vẫn bước tiếp qua mọi khó khăn.

ko.L: [사랑은] 모든 것을 감싸고, 모든 것을 믿고, 모든 것을 소망하고, 모든 것을 견딥니다.
ko.B: 사랑이 감싸 주지 못할 것은 없습니다. 사랑은 언제나 믿고 언제나 소망하며, 무엇이든지 견뎌 냅니다.
ko.R: 사랑은 무엇이든지 감싸 줍니다. 무슨 일이 있어도 계속 믿고 계속 소망합니다. 어떤 어려움이 와도 끝까지 견딥니다.

pt.L: Todas as coisas suporta, todas as coisas crê, todas as coisas espera, todas as coisas aguenta.
pt.B: Não há nada que o amor não possa suportar, nem momento em que ele deixe de crer ou de esperar; não há nada que ele não aguente.
pt.R: O amor aguenta qualquer coisa. Ele continua acreditando e continua esperando, aconteça o que acontecer. Ele continua firme em todas as dificuldades.

decisions.choice: bears: puts up with whatever comes, as Paul says of himself in 9:12
alternatives: covers, does not expose the faults of others
decisions.reason: στέγει first meant to cover, as a roof covers and keeps out the rain, and so to bear up or to put up with something. In 9:12 Paul uses it for putting up with every hardship for the gospel's sake. Some read it here as "covers", keeping quiet about others' faults (compare 1 Peter 4:8), or as "protects"; but the last verb of the verse would then not be the only one about bearing hardship.

decisions.choice: believes, hopes: love does not give up trust and hope, in God and for others
alternatives: love always believes the best about people
decisions.reason: πιστεύει does not mean that love believes anything it is told; Paul calls for testing what is said (12:10; 14:29). Love keeps trusting God and is ready to think the best of others, and it keeps hoping for what God will do. The verbs prepare for verse 13, where faith and hope stand with love.

decisions.choice: all things: in every situation, with no limit
decisions.reason: πάντα stands first four times for emphasis. It describes how far love goes, not a rule that love accepts every claim or every wrong (verse 6 says it takes no pleasure in wrongdoing).

decisions.choice: endures: holds out under hardship without giving way
decisions.reason: ὑπομένει is the verb of the noun for endurance (2 Corinthians 1:6; 6:4). Love does not give up when things go hard.

decisions.choice: All things it bears, all things it believes ... (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order, which puts "all things" first each time for emphasis (m3).

decisions.choice: There is nothing love cannot bear ... (B); puts up with anything ... keeps going through every trouble (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "all things" as English says it, and turn the verbs into plain words for bearing, trusting, hoping and holding out (m1-m4). "Believing" keeps the key term.

decisions.choice: sobrellevar ... resistir
decisions.reason: The first verb is putting up with whatever comes (m1), the last holding out under hardship (m4). Spanish keeps two different verbs for the two Greek words, "sobrellevar" and "resistir".

decisions.choice: Yote huyabeba, yote huyaamini ...
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "all things" first, as the Greek and the English Literal do; Swahili marks the fronted object with the object marker -ya- in each verb.

decisions.choice: "Mọi sự [tình yêu thương] đều ..." (L), the object first, with the subject bracketed
alternatives: "Tình yêu thương gánh chịu mọi sự"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order, which puts "all things" first four times, as the English does; Vietnamese can front the object with "đều", but needs the subject, which Literal brackets.

decisions.choice: "감싸다" for the first verb; "소망하다" for hope
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the first verb as bearing up under whatever comes, from a word for a roof that covers; "감싸다" (wrap round, shelter) keeps the picture of covering and bearing. "소망" is the word for hope in Romans, and returns in verse 13.

en.B: Love never comes to an end.

es.B: El amor nunca llega a su fin.
es.R: El amor nunca dejará de existir.

vi.L: Tình yêu thương không bao giờ sụp đổ.
vi.B: Tình yêu thương không bao giờ chấm dứt.
vi.R: Tình yêu thương sẽ không bao giờ ngừng.

pt.B: O amor nunca chega ao fim.
pt.R: O amor não vai ter fim.

decisions.choice: never falls: never collapses or comes to an end
decisions.reason: πίπτει means to fall. Set against the gifts that will be set aside (verses 8-10), it means that love never falls away or passes out of use. It could also mean that love never fails in what it does, but the contrast with what ends points to lasting.

decisions.choice: falls, as the SBLGNT reads
decisions.reason: From general knowledge: many later manuscripts read a compound form of the same verb, "falls away", with the same meaning. Reviewers must check the SBLGNT apparatus before this sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: comes to an end (B); will never stop (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "never falls" means here (m1). Literal keeps "falls".

source.text: εἴτε δὲ προφητεῖαι, καταργηθήσονται· εἴτε γλῶσσαι, παύσονται· εἴτε γνῶσις, καταργηθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: Whether but prophecies, they will be set aside; whether tongues, they will cease; whether knowledge, it will be set aside.

en.L: But if [there are] prophecies, they will be set aside; if tongues, they will cease; if knowledge, it will be set aside.
en.B: But prophecies will be done away with; tongues will fall silent; knowledge will be done away with.
en.R: But prophecy is not going to last. Speaking in tongues will stop. The gift of knowledge is not going to last.

fr.L: Mais s’[il y a] des prophéties, elles seront abolies ; s’[il y a] des langues, elles cesseront ; s’[il y a] de la connaissance, elle sera abolie.
fr.B: Mais les prophéties disparaîtront ; les langues se tairont ; la connaissance disparaîtra.
fr.R: Mais la prophétie ne va pas durer. On cessera de parler en langues. Le don de connaissance ne va pas durer.

es.L: Pero si [hay] profecías, quedarán anuladas; si lenguas, cesarán; si conocimiento, quedará anulado.
es.B: Pero las profecías llegarán a su fin; las lenguas callarán; el conocimiento llegará a su fin.
es.R: Pero la profecía no va a durar. Hablar en lenguas se acabará. El don de conocimiento no va a durar.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa kuna unabii, utawekwa kando; ikiwa lugha, zitakwisha; ikiwa maarifa, yatawekwa kando.
sw.B: Lakini unabii utaondolewa; lugha zitanyamaza; maarifa yataondolewa.
sw.R: Lakini unabii hautadumu. Kunena kwa lugha kutakoma. Karama ya maarifa haitadumu.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu [có] những lời tiên tri, chúng sẽ bị bãi bỏ; nếu [có] những tiếng lạ, chúng sẽ ngưng; nếu [có] tri thức, nó sẽ bị bãi bỏ.
vi.B: Nhưng những lời tiên tri sẽ bị loại bỏ; những tiếng lạ sẽ im bặt; tri thức sẽ bị loại bỏ.
vi.R: Nhưng lời tiên tri sẽ không còn mãi. Việc nói tiếng lạ sẽ ngưng. Ân tứ tri thức cũng sẽ không còn mãi.

ko.L: 그러나 예언들이 있어도 없어질 것이고, 방언들이 있어도 그칠 것이고, 지식이 있어도 없어질 것입니다.
ko.B: 그러나 예언도 사라지고, 방언도 그치고, 지식도 사라질 것입니다.
ko.R: 그러나 예언은 오래가지 않을 것입니다. 방언으로 말하는 일도 멈출 것입니다. 지식의 은사도 오래가지 않을 것입니다.

pt.L: Mas, se [há] profecias, serão postas de lado; se línguas, cessarão; se conhecimento, será posto de lado.
pt.B: Mas as profecias terão fim; as línguas vão se calar; o conhecimento terá fim.
pt.R: Mas a profecia não vai durar. Falar em línguas vai acabar. O dom do conhecimento não vai durar.

decisions.choice: whether there are prophecies, tongues or knowledge: whatever gifts there may be, all of them are temporary
decisions.reason: εἴτε repeated three times sets the gifts side by side: however much of them there is, each will end. They are three of the gifts named in 12:8-10 and in verses 1-2.

decisions.choice: will be set aside: will be brought to an end, no longer in use, with God as the one who ends them
decisions.reason: καταργηθήσονται is passive and is the verb Paul uses for what God brings to an end (1:28; 2:6; 15:24, 26). It returns in verse 10 for the partial and in verse 11 for childhood. The gifts are not bad; they belong to the present time.

decisions.choice: will cease: will stop
alternatives: tongues will stop of their own accord, earlier than the other gifts
decisions.reason: Paul uses a different verb for tongues, παύσονται. Some read the middle voice as meaning that tongues will die out of themselves, before the others; but Paul probably varies the verb for style, and verse 10 gives one time for all the partial gifts to end.

decisions.choice: knowledge: the gift of 12:8, knowledge of God's ways given by the Spirit
decisions.reason: Not all knowing ends (verse 12 promises full knowledge); what ends is the partial knowledge given now (verse 9).

decisions.choice: set aside (L); done away with (B); not going to last (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as for this verb in 2 Corinthians 3, so that readers can follow it; it returns in verses 10 and 11.

decisions.choice: speaking in tongues; the gift of knowledge
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the gifts are meant (m4).

decisions.choice: abolir (L); disparaître (B); ne pas durer (R) (also verses 10 and 11)
decisions.reason: The same French for this verb each time it returns in the chapter, so that readers can follow it, as the English does. "Abolir" keeps the sense of being brought to an end by another (m2); Balanced says plainly that the gifts will no longer be there, and Readable that they are not going to last.

decisions.choice: quedarán anuladas (L); llegarán a su fin (B); no va a durar (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means brought to an end, no longer in use (m2). Each level keeps one Spanish phrase for it in verses 8, 10 and 11, as the English keeps "set aside", "done away with" and "not going to last".

decisions.choice: kuwekwa kando (L); kuondolewa (B); hautadumu (R)
decisions.reason: The same words for katargeo here and in verses 10-11, following the English "set aside / done away with / not going to last"; "kubatilika" (be annulled) sounds like a legal verdict.

decisions.choice: "bị bãi bỏ" (L); "bị loại bỏ" (B); "sẽ không còn mãi" (R) for katargeo in 13:8-11
decisions.reason: The levels follow the English; one Vietnamese verb is kept at each level for the one Greek verb in verses 8, 10 and 11, so that the reader hears it return. The gifts keep their names from 12:8-10.

decisions.choice: "없어지다" (L); "사라지다" (B); "오래가지 않다" (R), here and in verses 10-11; "그치다" for tongues
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as being brought to an end by God, the verb of 1:28, 2:6 and 15:24-26; Korean keeps one verb for it through verses 8-11, and a different one for tongues, as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: postas de lado (L); terão fim (B); não vai durar (R)
decisions.reason: One wording per level for this verb in verses 8, 10 and 11, as the English keeps it, so the reader can follow it: Literal "pôr de lado"; Balanced "ter fim" ("abandonei" in verse 11, where Paul himself is the subject); Readable "não vai durar".

source.text: ἐκ μέρους γὰρ γινώσκομεν καὶ ἐκ μέρους προφητεύομεν·

records.literal_gloss: In part for we know and in part we prophesy;

en.L: For in part we know, and in part we prophesy.
en.B: For what we know is only partial, and our prophesying is partial too.
en.R: What we know now is not complete. What we say when we prophesy is not complete either.

fr.L: Car en partie nous connaissons, et en partie nous prophétisons ;
fr.B: Car ce que nous connaissons n’est que partiel, et nos prophéties aussi sont partielles.
fr.R: Ce que nous connaissons maintenant n’est pas complet. Ce que nous disons quand nous prophétisons n’est pas complet non plus.

es.L: Porque en parte conocemos y en parte profetizamos;
es.B: Porque lo que conocemos es solo parcial, y nuestro profetizar también es parcial.
es.R: Lo que sabemos ahora no está completo. Lo que decimos cuando profetizamos tampoco está completo.

sw.L: Kwa maana kwa sehemu tunajua, na kwa sehemu tunatoa unabii.
sw.B: Kwa maana tunachokijua ni sehemu tu, na unabii wetu pia ni sehemu tu.
sw.R: Tunachokijua sasa hakijakamilika. Tunachosema tunapotoa unabii nacho hakijakamilika.

vi.L: Vì chúng ta biết một phần và chúng ta nói tiên tri một phần;
vi.B: Vì những gì chúng ta biết chỉ là một phần, và lời tiên tri của chúng ta cũng chỉ là một phần.
vi.R: Những gì chúng ta biết bây giờ chưa đầy đủ. Những gì chúng ta nói khi nói tiên tri cũng chưa đầy đủ.

ko.L: 우리는 부분적으로 알고 부분적으로 예언하기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 우리가 아는 것은 부분일 뿐이고, 우리가 하는 예언도 부분일 뿐입니다.
ko.R: 지금 우리가 아는 것은 완전하지 않습니다. 우리가 예언하는 것도 완전하지 않습니다.

pt.L: Pois é em parte que conhecemos, e em parte que profetizamos.
pt.B: Pois o que conhecemos é só parcial, e as nossas profecias também são parciais.
pt.R: O que sabemos agora não é completo. O que dizemos quando profetizamos também não é completo.

decisions.choice: in part: partially, incompletely
decisions.reason: ἐκ μέρους means "in part". In 12:27 the same phrase meant "individually"; here it is set against the complete of verse 10, so it means that what we know and prophesy is not the whole.

decisions.choice: we know, we prophesy: all believers, Paul included
decisions.reason: Paul includes himself, an apostle with many gifts (14:18). Even the best knowledge and prophecy now given is partial.

decisions.choice: in part we know, and in part we prophesy (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order, which puts "in part" first for emphasis.

source.text: ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ τὸ τέλειον, τὸ ἐκ μέρους καταργηθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: When but comes the complete, the in part will be set aside.

en.L: But when the complete comes, what is in part will be set aside.
en.B: But when what is complete arrives, what is partial will be done away with.
en.R: But when what is complete comes, the things that are only partial are not going to last.

fr.L: Mais quand viendra ce qui est complet, ce qui est en partie sera aboli.
fr.B: Mais quand ce qui est complet arrivera, ce qui est partiel disparaîtra.
fr.R: Mais quand ce qui est complet viendra, les choses qui ne sont que partielles ne vont pas durer.

es.L: Pero cuando venga lo completo, lo que es en parte quedará anulado.
es.B: Pero cuando llegue lo que es completo, lo parcial llegará a su fin.
es.R: Pero cuando llegue lo que es completo, las cosas que son solo parciales ya no van a durar.

sw.L: Lakini kitakapokuja kilicho kamili, kilicho cha sehemu kitawekwa kando.
sw.B: Lakini kile kilicho kamili kitakapofika, kile kilicho cha sehemu kitaondolewa.
sw.R: Lakini kile kilicho kamili kitakapokuja, mambo yaliyo ya sehemu tu hayatadumu.

vi.L: nhưng khi điều trọn vẹn đến, thì điều [chỉ có] một phần sẽ bị bãi bỏ.
vi.B: Nhưng khi điều trọn vẹn đến, thì điều chỉ là một phần sẽ bị loại bỏ.
vi.R: Nhưng khi điều trọn vẹn đến, những điều chỉ có một phần sẽ không còn nữa.

ko.L: 그러나 완전한 것이 오면 부분적인 것은 없어질 것입니다.
ko.B: 그러나 완전한 것이 오면, 부분적인 것은 사라질 것입니다.
ko.R: 그러나 완전한 것이 오면, 부분적인 것은 더 이상 필요 없게 될 것입니다.

pt.L: Mas, quando vier o completo, o [que é] em parte será posto de lado.
pt.B: Mas, quando chegar o que é completo, o que é parcial terá fim.
pt.R: Mas, quando vier o que é completo, as coisas que são só parciais não vão durar.

decisions.choice: the complete: what is whole and finished, as opposed to what is in part
decisions.reason: τέλειον means complete, whole, or full-grown (2:6; 14:20). Here it is the opposite of ἐκ μέρους "in part" (verse 9), so "complete" is its sense; verse 11 adds the picture of growing up.

decisions.choice: the complete comes when Christ returns and believers see God face to face
decisions.reason: Verse 12 says when the partial ends: "then", when we see "face to face" and know as we are known. That points to the end of this age, when Christ comes (1:7-8; 15:23-28). Others have taken the complete to be the finished New Testament, or the church grown mature, or love itself; but the face to face sight of verse 12 is not yet given in this life.

decisions.choice: will be set aside: will come to an end, no longer needed
decisions.reason: καταργηθήσεται is the verb of verse 8. The partial gifts end not because they fail but because what they pointed to has come.

decisions.choice: the complete (L); what is complete (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Perfect" now suggests without fault; the Greek word here means whole, set against "in part" (m1). The footnote gives "the perfect".

decisions.choice: ce qui est complet
decisions.reason: As in English, "parfait" would suggest what is without fault; the Greek word here means what is whole, set against "en partie" (m1).

decisions.choice: lo completo
decisions.reason: The word means what is whole and finished, set against what is in part (m1). "Lo perfecto" would suggest without fault, so every level says "completo", as the English says "complete".

decisions.choice: "완전한 것" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word here as what is whole, set against "in part"; "완전한" says that plainly. It is the same Greek word as "the mature" (성숙한) of 2:6, where the sense is different.

source.text: ὅτε ἤμην νήπιος, ἐλάλουν ὡς νήπιος, ἐφρόνουν ὡς νήπιος, ἐλογιζόμην ὡς νήπιος· ὅτε γέγονα ἀνήρ, κατήργηκα τὰ τοῦ νηπίου.

records.literal_gloss: When I was a child, I used to speak as a child, I used to think as a child, I used to reason as a child; when I have become a man, I have set aside the [things] of the child.

en.L: When I was a child, I used to speak like a child, I used to think like a child, I used to reason like a child; now that I have become a man, I have set aside the [things] of the child.
en.B: When I was a child, I talked as a child talks, thought as a child thinks, and reasoned as a child reasons. But I am a man now, and I have done away with childish ways.
en.R: When I was a little child, I spoke, thought and reasoned the way little children do. But now I am grown up, and I have stopped acting like a child.

fr.L: Quand j’étais enfant, je parlais comme un enfant, je pensais comme un enfant, je raisonnais comme un enfant ; maintenant que je suis devenu un homme, j’ai aboli ce qui était de l’enfant.
fr.B: Quand j’étais enfant, je parlais comme parle un enfant, je pensais comme pense un enfant, je raisonnais comme raisonne un enfant. Mais maintenant je suis un homme, et j’ai fait disparaître les manières de l’enfance.
fr.R: Quand j’étais un petit enfant, je parlais, je pensais et je raisonnais comme les petits enfants. Mais maintenant je suis adulte, et j’ai arrêté d’agir comme un enfant.

es.L: Cuando yo era niño, hablaba como niño, pensaba como niño, razonaba como niño; ahora que he llegado a ser hombre, he dejado a un lado lo de niño.
es.B: Cuando era niño, hablaba como habla un niño, pensaba como piensa un niño y razonaba como razona un niño. Pero ahora soy hombre, y he dejado atrás las cosas de niño.
es.R: Cuando era pequeño, hablaba, pensaba y razonaba como lo hacen los niños pequeños. Pero ahora soy adulto, y he dejado de actuar como un niño.

sw.L: Nilipokuwa mtoto mchanga, nilikuwa nikisema kama mtoto mchanga, nilikuwa nikifikiri kama mtoto mchanga, nilikuwa nikiwaza kama mtoto mchanga; sasa kwa kuwa nimekuwa mwanamume, nimeyaweka kando mambo ya mtoto mchanga.
sw.B: Nilipokuwa mtoto, nilizungumza kama mtoto anavyozungumza, nilifikiri kama mtoto anavyofikiri, na nilipima mambo kama mtoto anavyopima. Lakini sasa mimi ni mwanamume mzima, nami nimeziondoa tabia za kitoto.
sw.R: Nilipokuwa mtoto mdogo, nilizungumza, nilifikiri na kupima mambo kama watoto wadogo wanavyofanya. Lakini sasa nimekua, nami nimeacha kutenda kama mtoto.

vi.L: Khi tôi còn là trẻ thơ, tôi đã nói như trẻ thơ, suy nghĩ như trẻ thơ, lý luận như trẻ thơ; khi tôi đã thành người lớn, tôi đã bỏ những điều thuộc về trẻ thơ.
vi.B: Khi tôi còn là một đứa trẻ, tôi nói như trẻ con nói, suy nghĩ như trẻ con suy nghĩ, và lý luận như trẻ con lý luận. Nhưng bây giờ tôi là người lớn, và tôi đã loại bỏ những điều trẻ con.
vi.R: Khi tôi còn bé, tôi nói, nghĩ và lý luận theo cách của trẻ con. Nhưng bây giờ tôi đã lớn, và tôi đã thôi cư xử như một đứa trẻ.

ko.L: 내가 어린아이였을 때에는 어린아이처럼 말하고, 어린아이처럼 생각하고, 어린아이처럼 따졌지만, 어른이 된 지금은 어린아이의 일들을 그만두었습니다.
ko.B: 내가 어린아이였을 때에는 어린아이처럼 말하고, 어린아이처럼 생각하고, 어린아이처럼 판단했습니다. 그러나 어른이 된 지금은 어린아이 같은 것들을 버렸습니다.
ko.R: 내가 어린아이였을 때에는 어린아이들이 하는 대로 말하고 생각하고 판단했습니다. 그러나 이제 나는 다 자랐고, 어린아이처럼 행동하는 일을 그만두었습니다.

pt.L: Quando eu era criança, falava como criança, pensava como criança, raciocinava como criança; agora que me tornei homem, pus de lado as [coisas] da criança.
pt.B: Quando eu era criança, falava como fala uma criança, pensava como pensa uma criança e raciocinava como raciocina uma criança. Mas agora sou homem, e abandonei os modos de criança.
pt.R: Quando eu era pequeno, eu falava, pensava e raciocinava do jeito que as crianças pequenas fazem. Mas agora sou adulto e parei de agir como criança.

decisions.choice: child: a young child, not yet grown
decisions.reason: νήπιος is a small child or infant, the word Paul used in 3:1 for the Corinthians as "infants in Christ". Here it is used without blame: every adult was once a child.

decisions.choice: I used to speak, think and reason; I have become, I have set aside: the past habits of childhood against a lasting change
decisions.reason: The first three verbs are imperfects, describing what a child does again and again. γέγονα and κατήργηκα are perfects: the change is complete and its result remains.

decisions.choice: think, reason: a child's outlook and the way it weighs things
alternatives: speak, think and reason correspond to tongues, prophecy and knowledge
decisions.reason: ἐφρόνουν is to think, to have a mind set on something; ἐλογιζόμην is to reason or count things up. Some see the three verbs as matching tongues, prophecy and knowledge in verse 8, but Paul does not say so.

decisions.choice: the picture explains verse 10: the present gifts belong to a time of growing up, and the end will be like becoming an adult
decisions.reason: κατήργηκα is the verb of verses 8 and 10. Paul is not telling the Corinthians to put away the gifts now; in chapter 14 he tells them to seek them (14:1, 39). The present age compared with the age to come is like childhood compared with adulthood.

decisions.choice: a man (L, B), grown up (R); set aside (L), done away with (B), stopped (R)
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of himself, so "man" takes no gender setting; Readable says "grown up", the point of the picture. The verb has the wording used in verses 8 and 10; Readable says simply that he stopped acting like a child. Literal says "now that I have become" to show that both verbs of the second half are perfects (m2).

decisions.choice: imparfait for the habits of childhood ("je parlais", "je pensais"), passé composé for the lasting change ("je suis devenu", "j’ai aboli")
decisions.reason: French has the two tenses that the Greek contrasts here (m2): the imperfect for what Paul used to do, the passé composé for what has changed and stays changed.

decisions.choice: he dejado a un lado
decisions.reason: The verb is the one of verses 8 and 10. Here Paul himself sets childish ways aside, so Literal says "dejar a un lado", which Spanish uses for a person, as the English keeps "set aside".

decisions.choice: nilikuwa nikisema, nilikuwa nikifikiri, nilikuwa nikiwaza
decisions.reason: "Nilikuwa ni-ki-" gives the past habit of the Greek imperfect, set against the perfect "nimekuwa ... nimeyaweka kando".

decisions.choice: "người lớn" for aner here, with "đã bỏ" (L), "đã loại bỏ" (B) for katargeo
decisions.reason: Paul sets the child against the grown man; Vietnamese "người lớn" says grown up, which is the point, as the English Readable says. The verb at Balanced is the one of verses 8 and 10.

decisions.choice: "어른" for "man" at every level
decisions.reason: The Greek word for "man" here is set against "child", so Korean says "어른" (grown-up).

decisions.choice: criança
decisions.reason: "Criança" is a small child of either sex, which is what the Greek word means (m1); "menino" would make it a boy.

source.text: βλέπομεν γὰρ ἄρτι δι’ ἐσόπτρου ἐν αἰνίγματι, τότε δὲ πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον· ἄρτι γινώσκω ἐκ μέρους, τότε δὲ ἐπιγνώσομαι καθὼς καὶ ἐπεγνώσθην.

records.literal_gloss: We see for now through a mirror in a riddle, then but face to face; now I know in part, then but I will know fully just as also I was fully known.

en.L: For now we see through a mirror, in a riddle, but then face to face; now I know in part, but then I will know fully, just as I also was fully known.
en.B: For now we see by means of a mirror, as if in a riddle, but then we will see face to face. Now my knowledge is partial, but then I will know fully, as God has fully known me.
en.R: Right now it is as if we are looking into a mirror that does not show things clearly. But one day we will see face to face. Right now I know only part of what there is to know. But then I will know fully, in the same way that God already knows me fully.

fr.L: Car maintenant nous voyons à travers un miroir, en énigme, mais alors face à face ; maintenant je connais en partie, mais alors je connaîtrai pleinement, comme aussi j’ai été pleinement connu.
fr.B: Car maintenant nous voyons par le moyen d’un miroir, comme dans une énigme, mais alors nous verrons face à face. Maintenant ma connaissance est partielle, mais alors je connaîtrai pleinement, comme Dieu m’a pleinement connu.
fr.R: Pour le moment, c’est comme si nous regardions dans un miroir qui ne montre pas les choses clairement. Mais un jour, nous verrons face à face. Pour le moment, je ne connais qu’une partie de ce qu’il y a à connaître. Mais alors je connaîtrai pleinement, de la même façon que Dieu me connaît déjà pleinement.

es.L: Porque ahora vemos por medio de un espejo, en enigma, pero entonces cara a cara; ahora conozco en parte, pero entonces conoceré plenamente, así como también fui plenamente conocido.
es.B: Ahora vemos por medio de un espejo, como en un enigma, pero entonces veremos cara a cara. Ahora mi conocimiento es parcial, pero entonces conoceré plenamente, como Dios me ha conocido plenamente.
es.R: Ahora mismo es como si miráramos en un espejo que no muestra las cosas con claridad. Pero un día veremos cara a cara. Ahora conozco solo una parte de lo que hay que conocer. Pero entonces conoceré plenamente, de la misma manera que Dios ya me conoce plenamente.

sw.L: Kwa maana sasa tunaona kupitia kioo, katika fumbo, lakini wakati ule uso kwa uso; sasa najua kwa sehemu, lakini wakati ule nitajua kikamilifu, kama vile nami nilivyojulikana kikamilifu.
sw.B: Kwa maana sasa tunaona kwa njia ya kioo, kana kwamba ni katika fumbo, lakini wakati huo tutaona ana kwa ana. Sasa maarifa yangu ni ya sehemu tu, lakini wakati huo nitajua kikamilifu, kama Mungu alivyonijua kikamilifu.
sw.R: Sasa ni kana kwamba tunatazama katika kioo kisichoonyesha mambo waziwazi. Lakini siku moja tutaona ana kwa ana. Sasa najua sehemu tu ya yale yanayoweza kujulikana. Lakini wakati huo nitajua kikamilifu, kama vile Mungu ananijua kikamilifu tayari sasa.

vi.L: Vì bây giờ chúng ta thấy qua một tấm gương, như trong một câu đố, nhưng khi ấy thì mặt đối mặt; bây giờ tôi biết một phần, nhưng khi ấy tôi sẽ biết trọn vẹn, như chính tôi cũng đã được biết trọn vẹn.
vi.B: Vì bây giờ chúng ta thấy qua một tấm gương, như thể trong một câu đố, nhưng khi ấy chúng ta sẽ thấy mặt đối mặt. Bây giờ điều tôi biết chỉ là một phần, nhưng khi ấy tôi sẽ biết trọn vẹn, như Đức Chúa Trời đã biết tôi trọn vẹn.
vi.R: Ngay bây giờ, chúng ta giống như đang nhìn vào một tấm gương không cho thấy mọi vật rõ ràng. Nhưng một ngày kia, chúng ta sẽ thấy mặt đối mặt. Bây giờ tôi chỉ biết một phần những gì cần biết. Nhưng khi ấy tôi sẽ biết trọn vẹn, như Đức Chúa Trời đã biết tôi trọn vẹn.

ko.L: 지금 우리는 거울을 통하여 수수께끼 속에서 보지만, 그때에는 얼굴과 얼굴을 마주하여 [볼 것입니다]. 지금 나는 부분적으로 알지만, 그때에는 내가 온전히 알려진 것처럼 나도 온전히 알게 될 것입니다.
ko.B: 지금 우리는 거울에 비친 모습을 보듯이, 수수께끼를 보듯이 봅니다. 그러나 그때에는 얼굴을 마주하고 볼 것입니다. 지금 내가 아는 것은 부분적이지만, 그때에는 하나님께서 나를 온전히 아신 것처럼 나도 온전히 알게 될 것입니다.
ko.R: 지금 우리는 모든 것이 똑똑히 보이지 않는 거울을 들여다보고 있는 것과 같습니다. 그러나 언젠가 우리는 얼굴과 얼굴을 마주하고 볼 것입니다. 지금 나는 알아야 할 것 가운데 일부만 압니다. 그러나 그때에는 하나님께서 이미 나를 온전히 아시는 것처럼 나도 온전히 알게 될 것입니다.

pt.L: Pois agora vemos por meio de um espelho, em enigma, mas então face a face; agora conheço em parte, mas então conhecerei plenamente, assim como também fui plenamente conhecido.
pt.B: Pois agora vemos por meio de um espelho, como num enigma, mas então veremos face a face. Agora o meu conhecimento é parcial, mas então vou conhecer por completo, assim como Deus me conheceu por completo.
pt.R: Agora é como se estivéssemos olhando num espelho que não mostra as coisas com clareza. Mas um dia veremos face a face. Agora eu conheço só uma parte do que há para conhecer. Mas então vou conhecer tudo por completo, do mesmo jeito que Deus já me conhece por completo.

decisions.choice: a mirror: a polished metal mirror, which showed a real but indirect image
alternatives: a window of thin stone or glass
decisions.reason: Ancient mirrors were made of polished metal, often bronze, for which Corinth was well known. They showed a true image, but only a reflection, never the thing itself. The contrast is between seeing indirectly and seeing directly, not between a true and a false image.

decisions.choice: in a riddle ... face to face: an echo of God's words about Moses in Numbers 12:8
decisions.reason: In Numbers 12:8 God says that with Moses he speaks mouth to mouth, plainly and not in riddles; the Greek Old Testament uses the same noun as αἰνίγματι. Moses spoke with God "face to face" (Exodus 33:11). Now, Paul says, all believers see God only indirectly, as in a riddle; then they will see as Moses was given to see, and more.

decisions.choice: then: at the end, when Christ comes, believers will see God directly
decisions.reason: ἄρτι and τότε set the present age against the age to come (verse 10). Seeing "face to face" is the hope of seeing God himself (Matthew 5:8; 1 John 3:2; Revelation 22:4).

decisions.choice: I will know fully just as I was fully known: I will know God as fully as God has known me
decisions.reason: ἐπιγνώσομαι and ἐπεγνώσθην are formed from the verb for "know" in this verse with a prefix that strengthens it, set against "in part". The passive ἐπεγνώσθην has God as the one who knows, as in 8:3 and Galatians 4:9. God's knowledge of his people, which is also his choosing and love, comes first; their full knowledge of him is the goal.

decisions.choice: we will see (B, R); God has fully known me (B); God already knows me fully (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves out the verb in "then face to face" and the one who knows in "I was fully known"; Balanced and Readable supply them (m3, m4).

decisions.choice: through a mirror, in a riddle (L); by means of a mirror, as if in a riddle (B); a mirror that does not show things clearly (R)
decisions.reason: "Riddle" keeps the link with Numbers 12:8 (m2). The familiar "through a glass, darkly" of the King James Version used "glass" for a mirror; "darkly" is footnoted as the alternative.

decisions.choice: en enigma (L); como en un enigma (B)
decisions.reason: "Enigma" is a riddle, the word of Numbers 12:8 that the verse echoes (m2, footnoted); "oscuramente" would lose the allusion.

decisions.choice: ana kwa ana (B, R); uso kwa uso (L)
alternatives: uso kwa uso at every level
decisions.reason: "Ana kwa ana" is the everyday Swahili for face to face; Literal keeps the image of the face, which echoes Numbers 12:8 (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "qua một tấm gương, như trong một câu đố" (L), "như thể trong một câu đố" (B); "mặt đối mặt"
decisions.reason: The riddle keeps the echo of Numbers 12:8 (m2), which a word like "mập mờ" would lose; the wording is fresh, apart from the plain phrase "mặt đối mặt".

decisions.choice: "수수께끼" (L, B) for the riddle; "얼굴과 얼굴을 마주하여" (L), "얼굴을 마주하고" (B)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision hears an echo of Numbers 12:8, where God speaks with Moses plainly and not in riddles; Korean keeps "riddle" rather than "dimly" so the echo can be heard.

decisions.choice: em enigma (L); como num enigma (B)
decisions.reason: "Enigma" is the Portuguese word for a riddle and comes from the Greek word itself, so it keeps the link with Numbers 12:8 (m2). "Obscuramente" would give only the effect.

source.text: νυνὶ δὲ μένει πίστις, ἐλπίς, ἀγάπη· τὰ τρία ταῦτα, μείζων δὲ τούτων ἡ ἀγάπη.

records.literal_gloss: Now but remains faith, hope, love, the three these; greater but of these the love.

en.L: But now faith, hope, love remain, these three; but the greatest of these [is] love.
en.B: As things are, then, three things last: faith, hope and love. And of these three, the greatest is love.
en.R: So three things last: faith, hope and love. And the greatest of the three is love.

fr.L: Mais maintenant demeurent la foi, l’espérance, l’amour, ces trois [choses] ; mais la plus grande de celles-ci [est] l’amour.
fr.B: Ainsi, dans l’état présent des choses, trois choses durent : la foi, l’espérance et l’amour. Et des trois, la plus grande est l’amour.
fr.R: Trois choses durent donc : la foi, l’espérance et l’amour. Et la plus grande des trois, c’est l’amour.

es.L: Pero ahora permanecen fe, esperanza, amor, estas tres [cosas]; pero la mayor de estas [es] el amor.
es.B: Así que ahora estas tres cosas perduran: la fe, la esperanza y el amor. Y de estas tres, la más grande es el amor.
es.R: Así que hay tres cosas que permanecen: la fe, la esperanza y el amor. Y la más importante de las tres es el amor.

sw.L: Lakini sasa imani, tumaini, upendo vinabaki, vitu hivi vitatu; lakini kilicho kikuu kati ya hivi [ni] upendo.
sw.B: Basi kama mambo yalivyo, vitu vitatu vinadumu: imani, tumaini na upendo. Na kati ya vitu hivi vitatu, kilicho kikuu kabisa ni upendo.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo kuna vitu vitatu vinavyodumu: imani, tumaini na upendo. Na kikuu kuliko vyote vitatu ni upendo.

vi.L: Nhưng bây giờ còn lại đức tin, niềm hy vọng, tình yêu thương, ba điều này; nhưng điều lớn nhất trong những điều này [là] tình yêu thương.
vi.B: Vậy, hiện nay có ba điều còn tồn tại: đức tin, niềm hy vọng và tình yêu thương. Và trong ba điều ấy, điều lớn nhất là tình yêu thương.
vi.R: Vậy có ba điều tồn tại mãi: đức tin, niềm hy vọng và tình yêu thương. Và điều lớn nhất trong ba điều ấy là tình yêu thương.

ko.L: 이제 믿음, 소망, 사랑, 이 세 가지가 남아 있습니다. 그러나 이 가운데 가장 큰 것은 사랑입니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 지금 남는 것은 세 가지, 곧 믿음과 소망과 사랑입니다. 그리고 이 셋 가운데 가장 큰 것은 사랑입니다.
ko.R: 그러니 끝까지 남는 것은 믿음과 소망과 사랑, 이 세 가지입니다. 그리고 이 셋 가운데 가장 큰 것은 사랑입니다.

pt.L: Mas agora permanecem fé, esperança, amor, estas três [coisas]; mas a maior delas [é] o amor.
pt.B: Como as coisas são, então, três coisas duram: a fé, a esperança e o amor. E, das três, a maior é o amor.
pt.R: Por isso, três coisas duram: a fé, a esperança e o amor. E a maior das três é o amor.

decisions.choice: but now: as things are, in contrast with the gifts that end
decisions.reason: νυνὶ can mark time ("now, in this present life") or logic ("but as it is"), as in 12:18. Read as logic, faith, hope and love last beyond the end of the gifts, into the age to come. Read as time, they are what lasts now, before the end, and only love goes on forever, since faith will become sight and hope will be fulfilled (2 Corinthians 5:7; Romans 8:24). The contrast with the passing gifts of verse 8 favors the logical sense, but the other is possible.

decisions.choice: remain: last, continue, in contrast with the gifts that are set aside
decisions.reason: μένει means to stay or last (3:14; 2 Corinthians 3:11). It is singular, though it has three subjects: the three stand together as one whole.

decisions.choice: faith, hope and love: three marks of the Christian life that Paul often names together
decisions.reason: The same three appear in 1 Thessalonians 1:3 and 5:8, Galatians 5:5-6 and Colossians 1:4-5. Here πίστις is the faith of every believer, not the special gift of verse 2.

decisions.choice: the greatest: a comparative form used for the highest of three
decisions.reason: μείζων is the comparative form, "greater". In the Greek of Paul's day the comparative was often used for the highest of more than two, so with three items the sense is "the greatest".

decisions.choice: love is the greatest because it is God's own love and the goal of the others
decisions.reason: Paul does not say why. The chapter shows that love gives every gift its worth (verses 1-3) and never ends (verse 8). Faith and hope look to God; love is what God himself shows (Romans 5:5, 8), and faith itself works through love (Galatians 5:6).

decisions.choice: last (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Remain" (Literal) is kept for the form; Balanced and Readable use the plain word "last" (m2).

decisions.choice: the greatest of these [is] love (L); of these three, the greatest is love (B); the greatest of the three is love (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says this and little else can be said; the wording is familiar because it is close to the Greek. Literal brackets the verb the Greek leaves out.

decisions.choice: fe, esperanza, amor, no article
decisions.reason: Spanish can list nouns without the article, as the Greek does here, so Literal keeps the bare list.

decisions.choice: vinabaki (L); vinadumu (B, R)
decisions.reason: Class 8 agreement (vitu vitatu, vinabaki) joins the three as a group: "kilicho kikuu" (the greatest one) agrees with "vitu".

decisions.choice: "đức tin, niềm hy vọng, tình yêu thương"
decisions.reason: The three key terms in the words of the Vietnamese 1 Thessalonians 1:3 and Colossians 1:4-5, so the reader can see the three Paul names together; "niềm hy vọng" is the word of Romans 5:5.

decisions.choice: "믿음, 소망, 사랑" at every level; "남아 있다", "남다" for remain
decisions.reason: "믿음" and "소망" are the words of Romans and 1 Thessalonians 1:3; the meaning decision reads the verb as lasting, in contrast with the gifts that end, which "남다" (remain) says.
